extracted.intended_audience: scientists, students, and applicants for university jobs/scholarships (readers of Nature, UK)
extracted.subtask_description: Notices and advertisements detailing eligibility, application formalities, deadlines, and tenure conditions for university posts, scholarships, examinations, and memberships appearing in a scientific journal's announcements page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrance Scholarships — award basis
rubrics_metrics.description: Will be awarded on the results of the examination to be held in June.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Bedford College lists Reid Scholarship (Arts) and Henry Tate/Preiffer Scholarships (Science) to be awarded on examination results; full particulars available on application to the Principal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clift'Courtauld Scholarship — degree requirement and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must hold a degree or equivalent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Clift'Courtauld Scholarship of the value of £15 is to be offered for the session beginning October 1907. Candidates must hold a degree or equivalent; applications should reach the Head of the Training Department not later than July 1, 1907.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gartside Scholarships — nationality, age, tenure, and application materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates must be of British nationality, and over the age of 18 and under the age of 24 at the date of election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three scholarships may be awarded in June; tenable for two years. Value: £50 first year (spent at the University), and from £150 to £950 the second year (spent in study of subjects bearing on Commerce in the United States, Germany, or other countries approved by the electors). Candidates must send in their applications together with testimonials of good character and record of previous training on or before June 1 to the Registrar, from whom further particulars can be obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: George Henry Lewes Studentship — application timing & contact
rubrics_metrics.description: An election to the studentship takes place in June; applications should be made to Professor J. N. Langley.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should be sent to Professor J. N. Langley, Hadgar? Low, Cambridge, not later than the stated June deadline (text gives 'not later than June 04'); contact the named professor for particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Palmer Scholarship (Institution of Civil Engineers) — nominee eligibility and need
rubrics_metrics.description: The nominee must be the son of a Civil Engineer; he must be desirous of matriculating and subsequently graduating at the University of Cambridge; and his circumstances must be such as to need the help afforded by the Scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Scholarship is of the annual value of £40 and will be vacant at the end of September next; a copy of the regulations relative to the Scholarship may be had on application to the Secretary of the Institution of Civil Engineers, Great George Street, Westminster, S.W.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application form & testimonial requirements for council/university appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for certain posts must be made on specified forms and accompanied by testimonials; strict submission deadlines apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example (County of London assistant mistress): Applications should be made on Form 40 H.G., obtainable from the Office of the Council; must be returned not later than 10 a.m. on the stated date and accompanied by copies of three testimonials of recent date. Candidates applying by post should enclose a stamped and addressed envelope. (Text notes that conviction or similar matters will be held to be a disqualification.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree or equivalent as essential qualification for teaching posts
rubrics_metrics.description: University degree, or its equivalent, essential for certain Polytechnic/college teaching posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly stated for posts such as Science Mistress, Form Mistress, and other secondary/tertiary teaching appointments (Woolwich Polytechnic examples). Commencing salaries and increment schemes are given alongside the qualification requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching experience requirement for lecturer/assistant lecturer positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching experience and/or specific institutional experience required for certain assistant lecturer and departmental posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: First Assistant in the Physics Department requires a University degree and experience in a University College or Technical Institute; Assistant Lecturer in Physics and Electrical Engineering—'Teaching experience essential.' Commencing salaries are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines and contact points for examinations and course particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms of application and further particulars for examinations and courses are available from named registrars/registries and must be obtained/submitted as directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Final Examination in Biological Chemistry (commencing in October)—form of application and particulars from the Registrar, Institute of Chemistry, 30 Bloomsbury Square, London, W.C.; Advanced lectures at King's College: attendance free and no ticket required; other notices give addresses and office contacts for particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership terms for British Association for the Advancement of Science
rubrics_metrics.description: No technical qualification is required for admission as a Member or as an Associate; fees apply on admission and for attendance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members pay £1 on admission and £1 for any subsequent year in which they attend an Annual Meeting without further liability; Associates pay 5s for each Annual Meeting they attend. Ladies admitted on the same terms. Contact: A. Silva White, Assistant Secretary.
